preconditions.expression: 1 <= n <= 8 and isinstance(n, int) and 1 <= m <= 10**9 and isinstance(m, int)
preconditions.description: The input consists of integers n (number of words) and m (length of chainword), where n is between 1 and 8 inclusive, and m is between 1 and 10^9 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(word) <= 5 and isinstance(word, str) and word.islower() and word.isalpha() for word in words)
preconditions.description: The dictionary contains n distinct words, each consisting of 1 to 5 lowercase Latin letters.
The dictionary has exactly n distinct words, with no duplicates.

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the count of valid chainword instances modulo 998244353.

postconditions.expression: result == sum(1 for _ in generate_valid_instances(words, m)) % 998244353
postconditions.description: The result is the count of all valid chainword instances of length m, where each instance is a triple (string, first_hint, second_hint) such that: (1) the string is a concatenation of words from the dictionary (not necessarily distinct) forming a length-m string, (2) the first_hint is a segmentation of the string into words from the dictionary, (3) the second_hint is another segmentation of the same string into words from the dictionary, and (4) the two segmentations may or may not be identical.

postconditions.expression: all(len(word) <= m for word in words)
postconditions.description: All words in the dictionary are of length at most m, ensuring they can be part of a valid segmentation for any m >= 1.
